summary: Jinhua Jia is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Colorado Boulder under Paul W. Kroll and held posts at Harvard, Hong Kong Polytechnic University, and CU Boulder.
Jinling He is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Hiroki Okumura.
Jinping Liao is a scholar in Buddhist and Iranian and Central Asian studies who completed a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin.

Jinshi Fan works in archaeology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University under Bai Su (~1958–1963) and served as Director of the Dunhuang Academy (1984–2014) and part-time professor at Lanzhou University (~2004).

Jinzhang Peng was a scholar of archaeology and Buddhist studies. He served as deputy director of the Department of History at Wuhan University (~1976–1986) and as a research professor at the Dunhuang Academy (~1986–2020).
Jiro Abe was a Japanese philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1904–1907). He later held academic posts at Japan Women's University (~1913–1923) and Tohoku University (~1923–1945).

Jiro Kawakita was a scholar of Tibetology who studied at Kyoto University (~1940–1943). He held academic posts at the Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1967–1977), the University of Tsukuba (~1977–1985), and Chubu University (~1985–1990).

Jiro Murata was a scholar of history, Sinology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1917–1920) and held a post at the National Institute of Technology, Akashi College (~1962–1968).

Jiro Sugiyama studied at the University of Tokyo (~1950–1953) in archaeology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Tokyo National Museum (~1957–1979), Nagaoka University of Technology (~1979–1994), Bukkyo University (~1994–1996), and ICPBS (~1996–2004).
Jiryo Masuda was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Unrai Wogihara and held a post as professor at the University of Calcutta.

Jitendra Nath Banerjea was a scholar of Indology and archaeology. He studied under Hemchandra Raychaudhuri (~1916–1918) and served as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (~1952–1959).

Jitendra Nath Mohanty was an Indologist and philosopher who earned his PhD at Göttingen. He taught at Calcutta, Burdwan, The New School, Oklahoma, and Emory, and served as professor at Temple University (~1986–2011).
Jitsuaki Oshika is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Tohoku University (~1941–1944) and later served as a professor at Toyo University (~1968–1989).

Jitsuzo Kuwabara was a scholar of Sinology and history who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1892–1896). He held posts at Third Higher School, Tokyo Higher Normal School, and Kyoto Imperial University (1909–1930).
Jiun Kubota is a religious and Buddhist studies figure who studied under and succeeded traditional teacher Kyozo Yamada (~1965–1989).

Jivnesh Sandhan works in computational linguistics and Indology. He completed his PhD at IIT Kanpur under Laxmidhar Behera and held posts at UC Berkeley, Kyoto University, IIT Kanpur, and IIT Dharwad (attested 2025).

Jiyu Ren studied at Peking University under Yongtong Tang and Lin He. He taught at Peking University (1942–1964) and directed the Institute of World Religions (~1964–1985) and the National Library of China (1987–2005).
Jo Khyab Pema Trinlé Nyingpo studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Pema Wangchok Gyelpo.

Joachim Gentz works in Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. He was Junior Professor at the University of Göttingen and Reader (attested 2013) and Professor (attested 2026) at the University of Edinburgh.
Joachim Prandstetter is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who completed his Magister degree at the University of Vienna in 1994, having studied under Gerhard Oberhammer.
